sitdown.prompt: Production raster game animation sprite sheet; photorealistic cutout of the exact SAME small fluffy orange-brown and white dog in references. Reference photo identifies the real dog. Existing sprite reference establishes accepted straight-front camera, full-body standing/sitting/lying appearance, lighting and scale. Match the white forehead stripe, round dark eyes, brown nose, ears, white chest and paws. No cartoon, no 3D toy, no different breed. True transparent background. EXACTLY 16 separate full-body frames arranged in strict 4 columns by 4 rows, uniform square cells, read LEFT to RIGHT then TOP to BOTTOM. Make all 16 the SAME physical dog, SAME lens, SAME body scale, SAME horizontal front-paw center and SAME ground line relative to each cell. Leave 12% margins in every cell, all fur/tail/paws fully contained, no overlap. Do NOT enlarge low poses to fill cell. Image should be square, high resolution, sharp face and fine fur. This is ONE continuous motion split into 16 evenly spaced successive moments, NOT 16 independent designs or random poses. Facial identity, coat silhouette/texture, camera, lighting and torso width must stay extremely consistent. Gradual small changes between adjacent frames are the highest priority. MOTION: standing front-facing to sitting front-facing. Frame 1 exactly resembles the standing dog in top-left of the existing posture reference. Frames 2-15 progressively bend hind legs and lower haunches, with hips moving behind planted front feet, shoulders/chest moving smoothly downward just a little, tail settling at dog's right side. Frame 16 matches the fully seated upright dog at row1 col4 of posture reference. Front paws stay planted on SAME floor and fixed horizontal spacing through ALL frames; the dog naturally becomes shorter as it sits. Eyes open, face calmly happy, tongue small and consistent throughout. Each frame shows a DIFFERENT small intermediate amount of the SAME anatomical sitting motion. Include all SIXTEEN, including eight tiny increments between near-standing and half-sitting and eight toward fully sitting.
